stem: A patient asks a Massachusetts pharmacy to compound a non-hazardous version of a commercially available drug solely because the compounded version would cost less. The commercially available product otherwise meets the patient's needs, and the prescriber identifies no patient-specific clinical difference. Which statement best applies to the statutory compounding analysis?

choices.text: Lower price alone establishes the patient-specific significant difference needed for compounding the commercially available product.
The pharmacy may treat price as the significant difference only when the patient signs a waiver.
A difference in price alone does not constitute the patient-specific significant difference contemplated by the Massachusetts compounding definition.
The pharmacy must reclassify the preparation as sterile because it uses a commercially available product.
The pharmacy may compound solely for price whenever the quantity is less than a 30-day supply.
